intent.raw_query: Greece under $2000, beaches and local food, summer, flying from NYC

experiences.name: Sunset Sailing & Snorkeling Around Santorini Caldera
experiences.description: Join a small-group catamaran cruise departing in the late afternoon around the volcanic caldera of Santorini. Snorkel in crystal-clear Aegean waters, visit the Red and White beaches, and enjoy a traditional Greek mezze spread with local wine on board as you watch the legendary Oia sunset from the sea.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour (Varvakios Agora)
experiences.description: Explore the historic Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) with a local food guide in the cool morning hours. Taste cured meats, fresh cheeses, olives, loukoumades (honey donuts), and spanakopita. Learn about Greek culinary traditions and shop for local spices and ingredients. This indoor-friendly tour is perfect for avoiding midday heat.

experiences.name: Elafonissi Beach Morning Visit
experiences.description: Arrive early at the stunning Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete to enjoy its famous pink-tinged sand and shallow turquoise lagoons before the midday crowds and heat arrive. Wade across the shallow sandbar to the small island, collect sea glass, and swim in calm, warm waters. Pack a local picnic from a nearby bakery for a perfect morning escape.

experiences.name: Traditional Greek Cooking Class in a Cretan Village
experiences.description: Spend a morning in a family-run kitchen in a traditional Cretan village learning to prepare authentic dishes such as dakos (barley rusk salad), lamb with stamnagathi greens, and galaktoboureko (custard pastry). The class takes place indoors making it an ideal midday heat or rain alternative. Enjoy the meal you prepare with local raki and wine.

experiences.name: Evening Taverna Crawl in Nafplio Old Town
experiences.description: As temperatures cool in the evening, stroll through the charming Venetian old town of Nafplio and hop between traditional tavernas sampling local Peloponnesian specialties: grilled octopus, tomatokeftedes, fresh grilled fish, and local Nemea red wine. The cobblestone streets and neoclassical architecture create a magical atmosphere perfect for a leisurely evening of authentic Greek dining and culture.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Greece
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 14:50
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) at 14:50. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the X95 express bus or Metro Line 3 into central Athens — both budget-friendly options under €10. Check into your budget hostel or guesthouse in the Monastiraki or Psiri neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Take a relaxed evening stroll through Monastiraki Square and the Plaka neighborhood. Admire the illuminated Acropolis from street level. Grab a souvlaki wrap from a street vendor to kick off your Greek food experience.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or grab a snack at the airport
meals.lunch: Grab a quick gyro or tiropita (cheese pie) from a bakery near the airport or on arrival
meals.dinner: Street souvlaki wrap with tzatziki from a local kiosk in Monastiraki — around €2.50–€3.50

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 activities begin only after 14:50 arrival. Use the Metro Line 3 (€9 one-way) or X95 bus (€5.50) to reach central Athens. Book budget accommodation in Monastiraki or Psiri for easy access to sights.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Acropolis early (opens at 8:00 AM) to beat the crowds and heat. Explore the Parthenon, Erechtheion, and Propylaea. Combined ticket is €20 but covers multiple sites — excellent value. Bring water and sunscreen.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down to the Ancient Agora of Athens (included in the combined ticket). Explore the well-preserved Temple of Hephaestus and the Stoa of Attalos museum. Afterward, wander through the Monastiraki flea market for budget souvenirs and people-watching.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Psiri neighborhood for dinner. Explore the lively tavernas and ouzeries. Try a mezze spread with local wine or ouzo.

meals.breakfast: Spanakopita (spinach pie) and Greek coffee from a local bakery — €2–€3
meals.lunch: Souvlaki plate with pita, tomatoes, and onions from a local grill near Monastiraki — €5–€7
meals.dinner: Mezze platter (olives, feta, dolmades, grilled vegetables) at a Psiri taverna — €10–€14 per person

day_by_day.notes: The €20 combined Acropolis ticket covers 7 archaeological sites valid for 5 days — great budget value. Arrive at the Acropolis before 9:00 AM to avoid crowds. Wear comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Archaeological Museum (€12 entry, free on certain days). Marvel at the Antikythera Mechanism, Mycenaean gold artifacts, and ancient sculptures. One of the world's greatest museums and very affordable.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Exarchia neighborhood — Athens' bohemian quarter. Browse independent bookshops, street art, and local cafes. Visit the Strefi Hill park for a free panoramic view of Athens without the tourist crowds.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Thissio neighborhood for sunset views of the Acropolis from the outdoor cafes along Apostolou Pavlou pedestrian walkway. Enjoy a budget dinner at a local taverna.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt with honey and walnuts from a local café — €3–€4
meals.lunch: Horiatiki (Greek salad) and bread at a neighborhood taverna in Exarchia — €5–€7
meals.dinner: Grilled octopus or moussaka at a Thissio taverna — €10–€13 per person

day_by_day.notes: The National Archaeological Museum is free on the first Sunday of each month and for EU students. Exarchia is safe during the day and great for authentic local culture away from tourist traps.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early KTEL bus or train from Athens to Cape Sounion (about 1.5 hours, €7 one-way by bus from Pedion Areos). Visit the stunning Temple of Poseidon perched on a cliff above the Aegean Sea — entry €10.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at the small beach below Cape Sounion. The water is crystal clear and the setting is dramatic. Bring a packed lunch or buy from the small kiosk nearby. Swim and relax before heading back to Athens.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Athens by late afternoon. Rest and freshen up, then explore the Koukaki neighborhood near the Acropolis Museum for a local dinner experience.

meals.breakfast: Koulouri (sesame bread ring) and coffee from a street vendor — €1.50–€2
meals.lunch: Packed picnic from a local supermarket (cheese, olives, bread, fruit) — €4–€6
meals.dinner: Pastitsio (Greek baked pasta) or stuffed peppers at a Koukaki neighborhood restaurant — €9–€12

day_by_day.notes: The KTEL bus to Cape Sounion departs from Pedion Areos park in Athens. Check the schedule in advance. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and water — the cape is exposed and sunny. June temperatures average 23°C.

day_by_day.morning: Take the ferry from Piraeus port to Aegina island (about 1 hour by fast ferry, €14–€18 round trip). Aegina is one of the closest and most affordable Saronic islands from Athens. Explore Aegina Town's waterfront, neoclassical buildings, and the morning fish market.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle (€5–€8/day) or take a local bus to the Temple of Aphaia — a remarkably preserved ancient temple with sea views (€6 entry). Afterward, head to Agia Marina beach on the east coast for a swim in calm, clear waters.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Aegina Town for dinner at a waterfront taverna before catching the evening ferry back to Piraeus. Aegina is famous for its pistachios — buy a bag as a snack.

meals.breakfast: Tiropita and freddo espresso at a café in Piraeus before boarding — €3–€4
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled fish or calamari at a simple taverna near Agia Marina beach — €10–€14
meals.dinner: Grilled sardines and village salad at an Aegina Town waterfront taverna — €10–€13

day_by_day.notes: Ferries depart from Piraeus Gate E8/E9. Take Metro Line 1 (Green) from central Athens to Piraeus station (€1.40). Book return ferry in advance during June. Aegina pistachios make excellent budget snacks and gifts.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take the KTEL bus or train from Athens to Nafplio in the Peloponnese (about 2–2.5 hours, €13–€15 by bus from Kifissos terminal). Nafplio is a charming, romantic town and one of Greece's most beautiful — very budget-friendly compared to the islands.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check into a budget guesthouse in Nafplio's old town. Explore the Venetian old town on foot — wander the narrow lanes, visit Syntagma Square, and climb the 999 steps to the Palamidi Fortress for sweeping views of the Argolic Gulf (€8 entry).
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Nafplio waterfront promenade at sunset. Enjoy dinner at one of the affordable tavernas in the old town backstreets away from the main tourist strip.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at a bakery near the Athens bus terminal before departure — €3–€4
meals.lunch: Cheese pie and juice from a Nafplio bakery upon arrival — €3–€5
meals.dinner: Lamb chops or chicken souvlaki with roasted potatoes at a backstreet Nafplio taverna — €10–€14

day_by_day.notes: KTEL buses to Nafplio depart from Athens' Kifissos Bus Terminal A. Nafplio is an excellent base for exploring the Peloponnese. The Palamidi Fortress is best visited in the late afternoon for golden light and cooler temperatures.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Mycenae (about 30 minutes by local bus or taxi, €5–€8 one-way). Explore the legendary Bronze Age citadel — the Lion Gate, Treasury of Atreus (Tomb of Agamemnon), and the ancient ruins. Entry €12 or included in a combo ticket.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Nafplio and head to Arvanitia Beach — a small, rocky beach just a 10-minute walk from the old town. It's free, scenic, and perfect for a refreshing swim in the Argolic Gulf. Alternatively, take a short water taxi to the tiny Bourtzi castle island (€3 round trip).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a leisurely evening in Nafplio's old town. Browse the local shops for budget-friendly olive oil products and ceramics. Have dinner at a traditional ouzerie.

meals.breakfast: Greek coffee and a bougatsa (custard pastry) at a Nafplio café — €3–€4
meals.lunch: Packed snacks from a local supermarket eaten at Mycenae — €4–€6
meals.dinner: Mezze and ouzo at a traditional ouzerie in Nafplio — €10–€13

day_by_day.notes: Local buses run between Nafplio and Mycenae several times daily — check the schedule at the Nafplio bus station. Arvanitia Beach has a small café and changing facilities. The water taxi to Bourtzi runs from the main harbor.

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Nafplio to Thessaloniki by bus or train (long travel day — approximately 5–6 hours with connections via Athens or Corinth, €25–€35). Alternatively, take a scenic route via Corinth, stopping briefly to see the Corinth Canal.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Thessaloniki, Greece's vibrant second city. Check into a budget hostel in the city center near Aristotelous Square. Take a walk along the waterfront promenade (Nikis Avenue) and visit the iconic White Tower (€4 entry).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Ladadika district — Thessaloniki's historic warehouse quarter turned nightlife and dining hub. This is the perfect place to experience Thessaloniki's legendary food scene on a budget.

meals.breakfast: Grab a koulouri or tiropita at a bakery before departing Nafplio — €2–€3
meals.lunch: Snack on the bus or grab a quick bite at a rest stop — €4–€6
meals.dinner: Bougatsa (sweet or savory) and a beer at a Ladadika taverna — €8–€12

day_by_day.notes: Thessaloniki is known as Greece's food capital — it's a paradise for budget food lovers. The city has excellent street food, markets, and affordable restaurants. Consider an overnight bus to save on accommodation costs if budget is very tight.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Thessaloniki Archaeological Museum (€8 entry) — home to spectacular Macedonian gold treasures including finds from the royal tombs of Vergina. Then walk to the Byzantine Walls and the Trigonion Tower in the Ano Poli (Upper Town) neighborhood for panoramic city views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Modiano and Kapani covered markets — Thessaloniki's bustling central markets. Sample local specialties like taramosalata, local cheeses, and cured meats. Browse the stalls for budget-friendly local products. Visit the Rotunda, a UNESCO World Heritage Roman monument (free exterior viewing).
day_by_day.evening: Join locals for the traditional evening volta (stroll) along the waterfront. Enjoy dinner in the Navarinou Square area, popular with students and locals for affordable, quality food.

meals.breakfast: Thessaloniki-style bougatsa with cream filling at a famous local bougatsa shop — €2.50–€3.50
meals.lunch: Fresh produce, olives, and local cheese from Modiano Market — €5–€7
meals.dinner: Grilled meat platter (mixed grill) at a student-friendly taverna near Navarinou Square — €10–€13

day_by_day.notes: Thessaloniki's Ano Poli (Upper Town) is a charming, less-touristy neighborhood with Byzantine churches and traditional houses. The city's food scene is exceptional — try local specialties like trigona panoramatos (cream-filled pastry triangles).

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Vergina (about 1.5 hours by KTEL bus, €5–€7 one-way) to visit the Royal Tombs of Macedon — the burial site of Philip II, father of Alexander the Great. The underground museum is extraordinary (€12 entry). A true highlight of any Greece trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Thessaloniki by early afternoon. Visit the Thessaloniki waterfront and the sculpture of Alexander the Great. Relax at a café along the seafront and watch the boats. Explore the Bit Bazaar antique market in the old Jewish quarter.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Thessaloniki's famous nightlife and food culture. Head to the Valaoritou Street area for affordable bars and restaurants. Try local meze with tsipouro (Greek spirit similar to grappa).

meals.breakfast: Koulouri with sesame and a freddo cappuccino at a Thessaloniki café — €2.50–€3.50
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from the market or a quick gyro near the Vergina bus stop — €4–€6
meals.dinner: Tsipouro with meze (small plates of local food) at a traditional tsipouradiko — €10–€14

day_by_day.notes: KTEL buses to Vergina depart from Thessaloniki's main KTEL Macedonia bus station. The Royal Tombs museum is underground and air-conditioned — a welcome break from the heat. Book the morning bus to maximize time at the site.

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Thessaloniki to Halkidiki peninsula by KTEL bus (about 1–1.5 hours, €5–€8). Head to Kassandra peninsula — the closest and most accessible of Halkidiki's three 'fingers.' Check into a budget campsite or simple guesthouse near Kallithea or Nea Fokaia beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at one of Halkidiki's stunning beaches. Kallithea Beach is beautiful with clear turquoise water and a sandy shore. Swim, snorkel, and relax. The water temperature in June is perfect — around 22–24°C.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from the beach. Have dinner at a simple beachside taverna or grill house. Halkidiki is more affordable than the Aegean islands for beach holidays.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at a Thessaloniki bakery before the bus — €2–€3
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled fish or calamari at a beachside taverna — €10–€13
meals.dinner: Grilled chicken or pork souvlaki with salad at a local grill house — €8–€11

day_by_day.notes: Halkidiki offers some of Greece's best beaches without the island ferry costs. Budget campsites are available from €8–€12 per person per night. Bring snorkeling gear if you have it — the waters are crystal clear. June is ideal before the peak July–August crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Explore more of Halkidiki's coastline. Take a local bus or rent a bicycle to visit Sani Beach or Possidi Cape — a long sandy spit with shallow, calm waters ideal for swimming. The lighthouse at Possidi is a scenic landmark.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the village of Nea Fokaia and its Byzantine tower. Swim at the local beach and enjoy the relaxed pace of a Greek seaside village. Browse the small local shops for honey, olive oil, and local products at village prices.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your accommodation for a final Halkidiki evening. Enjoy a simple dinner at a local taverna with fresh seafood. Watch the stars from the beach — light pollution is minimal here.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt with local honey and fruit from a village shop — €3–€4
meals.lunch: Grilled octopus and village salad at a Possidi taverna — €10–€13
meals.dinner: Fresh mussels (Halkidiki is famous for them) with bread and local wine — €9–€12

day_by_day.notes: Halkidiki is famous for its mussel farming — try them steamed or saganaki (fried with cheese and tomato). Local honey and olive oil from village shops make excellent budget souvenirs. The beaches are less crowded on weekdays.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Greece. Return to Thessaloniki by KTEL bus (1–1.5 hours). If time allows, stop at the Thessaloniki Central Market one last time to pick up food souvenirs — vacuum-packed olives, local spices, tahini, and Greek coffee are all affordable and packable.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, visit any remaining Thessaloniki sights — the Church of Agios Dimitrios (free entry, stunning Byzantine mosaics) or simply relax at a waterfront café with a final Greek coffee. Head to Thessaloniki Airport (Macedonia Airport) for your return flight.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Reflect on 13 days of beaches, ancient history, and incredible local food across Athens, the Peloponnese, and northern Greece.

meals.breakfast: Final Greek breakfast — freddo espresso and a cheese pie at a Thessaloniki café — €3–€4
meals.lunch: Last souvlaki or gyro wrap from a local grill — €3–€5
meals.dinner: Airport meal or snacks purchased from the market — €5–€8

day_by_day.notes: Thessaloniki Airport (SKG) is about 15 km from the city center — take bus route 78 (€2) or a taxi (€15–€20). Allow at least 2 hours before departure. Total estimated budget for 13 days (excluding flights): €500–€700 per person, covering accommodation, transport, food, and entry fees.

trip_options.title: Classic Greece Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour (Varvakios Agora)
experiences.description: Explore the historic Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) with a local food guide in the cool morning hours. Taste cured meats, fresh cheeses, olives, loukoumades (honey donuts), and spanakopita. Learn about Greek culinary traditions and shop for local spices and ingredients. This indoor-friendly tour is perfect for avoiding midday heat.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival day – flight lands at 14:50, so morning is in transit. Rest and settle into accommodation after landing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) at 14:50. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the X95 express bus or Metro Line 3 to central Athens. Check into your mid-range hotel in the Monastiraki or Koukaki neighborhood. Take a gentle orientation stroll around Monastiraki Square and the Flea Market to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the atmospheric Plaka neighborhood, the oldest district in Athens. Explore the narrow cobblestone streets, browse local shops, and soak in the ambiance beneath the Acropolis lit up at night.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: Grab a quick gyros wrap from a street kiosk near Monastiraki Square (€3–5) after settling in
meals.dinner: Taverna Monastiri or a similar traditional taverna in Plaka – try moussaka, tzatziki, and a glass of local wine (€18–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light due to travel fatigue. Exchange some euros at the airport or use an ATM. Metro Line 3 from the airport to Monastiraki takes about 40 minutes and costs €9.

day_by_day.morning: Athens Central Market Food Tour (Varvakios Agora): Join the guided food tour of the historic Varvakios Agora starting early in the cool morning hours. Explore stalls overflowing with fresh fish, meat, spices, olives, and local cheeses with a knowledgeable local guide. Sample traditional Greek products and learn about Athenian food culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the nearby Monastiraki Flea Market and then head to the Ancient Agora of Athens – the heart of ancient Athenian civic life. Explore the well-preserved Stoa of Attalos museum and the Temple of Hephaestus (€10 entry). Enjoy views of the Acropolis from below.
day_by_day.evening: Head up to the Thissio neighborhood for sunset drinks at a rooftop café with Acropolis views. Then explore the trendy Psiri district for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Included in the food tour or grab a bougatsa (custard pastry) and Greek coffee at a local bakery near the market (€4–6)
meals.lunch: Taste samples from the food tour, supplemented by a souvlaki plate at a local grill near the Agora (€8–12)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mezedopoleio (meze restaurant) in Psiri – share small plates like grilled octopus, saganaki, and spanakopita (€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The food tour typically starts at 9:00–10:00 AM – book in advance. Wear comfortable walking shoes. The Ancient Agora is a 10-minute walk from Varvakios Agora.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Acropolis of Athens early (open from 8:00 AM) to beat the heat and crowds. Explore the Parthenon, Erechtheion, and Propylaea. Combined ticket (€30) includes entry to multiple archaeological sites. The views over Athens are spectacular in the morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Acropolis Museum (€15), one of Greece's finest museums, housing original sculptures and artifacts from the Acropolis. Afterward, stroll through the Koukaki neighborhood – a local, less touristy area with charming cafés and boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Take the funicular up Lycabettus Hill for panoramic sunset views over Athens and the Aegean. Enjoy a drink at the hilltop café before descending for dinner in the Kolonaki neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt with honey and walnuts at a café near your hotel (€5–7)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Acropolis Museum café with views of the Parthenon (€12–16)
meals.dinner: Dinner in Kolonaki – try a modern Greek restaurant offering creative takes on traditional dishes like lamb kleftiko or fresh grilled sea bream (€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at the Acropolis by 8:00–8:30 AM to avoid peak crowds and heat. Bring water and sunscreen. The funicular (Τελεφερίκ) costs €7 return.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Cape Sounion: Take a KTEL bus from Pedion Areos (€6.50 each way, ~1.5 hours) to the stunning Temple of Poseidon perched on a cliff above the Aegean Sea. Explore the ancient ruins and enjoy breathtaking coastal views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at the beautiful beaches near Sounion or stop at Vouliagmeni Beach on the return journey – a popular Athenian Riviera beach with clear blue water and beach facilities (€8–10 entry). Swim and relax in the warm June sea.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Athens by early evening. Relax and freshen up, then enjoy a leisurely dinner in the Pangrati neighborhood – a local favorite away from tourist crowds.

meals.breakfast: Grab a tiropita (cheese pie) and coffee from a bakery before catching the bus (€4–5)
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a taverna near Cape Sounion – grilled fish, Greek salad, and local wine (€20–28 per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a neighborhood taverna in Pangrati – try slow-cooked lamb or stuffed vegetables (gemista) with local retsina wine (€16–22 per person)

day_by_day.notes: KTEL buses to Sounion depart from Pedion Areos Park approximately every hour. The Temple of Poseidon entry is €10. Bring a beach towel and snorkeling gear if you have them.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day to Santorini: Take a taxi or Metro to Piraeus Port (or a ferry from Rafina) and board a high-speed ferry to Santorini (Thira). High-speed ferries take approximately 5–6 hours; book in advance (€50–80 per person). Enjoy the Aegean scenery from the deck.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Santorini at Athinios Port. Take a local bus or shared taxi to Fira (the island's capital). Check into your mid-range hotel or guesthouse in Fira or nearby Firostefani. Explore Fira's winding streets, boutiques, and caldera-edge walkways.
day_by_day.evening: Walk the caldera path from Fira toward Firostefani for stunning sunset views over the volcanic caldera. Enjoy dinner at a caldera-view restaurant in Fira.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the port or on the ferry (€5–8)
meals.lunch: Snack on the ferry – bring your own food or buy from the onboard café (€8–12)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range restaurant in Fira with caldera views – try fresh grilled octopus, fava (yellow split pea dip), and local Assyrtiko white wine (€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book ferry tickets at least a few days in advance, especially in June. Seajets and Hellenic Seaways offer fast ferry services. Confirm ferry departure times from Piraeus or Rafina.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Oia village: Take the local bus (€1.80) or rent an ATV (€25–35/day) to the iconic village of Oia in northern Santorini. Wander the blue-domed churches, whitewashed alleys, and art galleries in the cooler morning hours before the crowds arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head down to Ammoudi Bay below Oia – a tiny fishing harbor accessible by 300 steps or donkey path. Swim in the crystal-clear water directly off the volcanic rocks and enjoy the secluded cove atmosphere. Alternatively, visit Armeni Beach nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Oia for the world-famous Santorini sunset – arrive at least 1 hour early to secure a good viewing spot. The sunset over the caldera from Oia is one of the most spectacular in the world.

meals.breakfast: Greek breakfast at your hotel or a café in Fira – eggs, local tomatoes, olives, and feta (€8–12)
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at one of the tavernas at Ammoudi Bay – grilled lobster pasta or fresh catch of the day (€22–30 per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner in Oia after the sunset – try a mid-range restaurant serving Santorinian specialties like white eggplant, cherry tomato fritters, and local capers (€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Oia gets extremely crowded at sunset. Arrive by 7:00 PM minimum for a good spot. The ATV rental gives you flexibility to explore the island at your own pace.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the prehistoric site of Akrotiri – a remarkably preserved Minoan Bronze Age settlement buried by the volcanic eruption of 1627 BC (entry €12). Often called the 'Pompeii of the Aegean,' it offers fascinating insight into ancient island life. Visit early before the heat builds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at Red Beach (Kokkini Paralia) near Akrotiri – one of Santorini's most dramatic beaches with striking red and black volcanic cliffs. Swim in the turquoise water and relax on the unique colored sand. Nearby White Beach and Black Beach (Perissa or Perivolos) are also excellent options.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Fira for the evening. Explore the local wine scene – Santorini is famous for its volcanic-soil wines, particularly Assyrtiko. Visit a wine bar for a tasting flight of local varieties.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a local bakery in Fira – fresh bread, honey, and Greek coffee (€5–7)
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at a beach taverna near Red Beach – Greek salad, grilled sardines, and cold Mythos beer (€14–18 per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range restaurant in Fira – try the Santorinian beef stew (stifado) or fresh pasta with local seafood, paired with Assyrtiko wine (€22–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Red Beach requires a short 10-minute walk over rocky terrain – wear sturdy sandals. The path can be slippery. Akrotiri is a must-see; combine it with the beach for an efficient day.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day to Mykonos: Take a high-speed ferry from Santorini to Mykonos (approximately 2–3 hours, €40–65 per person). Book in advance. Enjoy the Cycladic island scenery during the crossing. Arrive and check into your mid-range hotel in Mykonos Town (Chora).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Mykonos Town (Chora): Wander the iconic labyrinthine whitewashed alleys, discover the famous windmills on the hill above Little Venice, and explore the charming waterfront area of Little Venice with its colorful balconies hanging over the sea.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the vibrant atmosphere of Mykonos Town in the evening. Stroll along the waterfront, watch the pelicans (Mykonos's famous mascots) near the old port, and settle in for dinner at a local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast on the ferry or at the port before departure (€5–8)
meals.lunch: Upon arrival in Mykonos, grab a quick lunch at a local gyros shop in Chora (€5–8)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a traditional Greek taverna in Mykonos Town – try fresh grilled fish, loukoumades (honey donuts) for dessert, and local wine (€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Mykonos is more expensive than other Greek islands. Mid-range dining and accommodation will cost slightly more here. Book ferry tickets well in advance for June travel.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Delos Island: Take the short boat trip (€20 return, 30 minutes) from Mykonos Old Port to the sacred island of Delos – one of the most important archaeological sites in Greece and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Explore the ancient ruins of temples, mosaics, and the famous Terrace of the Lions (entry €12).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Mykonos by early afternoon. Head to one of Mykonos's famous beaches – Platis Gialos is a good mid-range option with beach bars, sunbeds, and clear water. Alternatively, Paradise Beach offers a livelier atmosphere. Relax, swim, and enjoy the June sunshine.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Mykonos Town for the evening. Explore the boutique shops and art galleries, then enjoy sundowners at a Little Venice bar watching the sunset over the Aegean.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt parfait and coffee at a café in Mykonos Town before the Delos boat (€7–10)
meals.lunch: Pack a light snack for Delos (no restaurants on the island) or eat at the small café there (€8–12)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a seafood restaurant near the old port in Mykonos Town – fresh lobster spaghetti or grilled sea bass (€28–38 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Delos boats depart from the Old Port at 9:00 AM and 10:00 AM; last return is around 3:00 PM. Bring water, sunscreen, and a hat – there is very little shade on Delos. The site is extensive; allow 2–3 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a scooter or ATV (€25–40/day) and explore the quieter, less-visited beaches on the northern and eastern sides of Mykonos. Agios Sostis Beach is a beautiful, undeveloped beach with no sunbeds – bring your own towel. Panormos Bay is another serene option with crystal-clear water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the island's interior – visit the traditional village of Ano Mera with its 16th-century Panagia Tourliani Monastery. Browse the local market and enjoy the authentic, non-touristy atmosphere of this inland village.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Mykonos Town for a final evening on the island. Enjoy a leisurely dinner and perhaps a cocktail at one of the stylish bars in the Kastro area.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel or a local café – fresh orange juice, eggs, and toast (€8–12)
meals.lunch: Lunch at the only taverna at Agios Sostis Beach (Kiki's Tavern – cash only, no reservations, arrive early) – grilled meats and salads (€15–20 per person)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner in Mykonos Town – try a mezze spread with various dips, grilled halloumi, and fresh calamari at a mid-range taverna (€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Kiki's Tavern at Agios Sostis is legendary but has long queues – arrive before noon. Cash only. The northern beaches are much quieter and more beautiful than the famous southern party beaches.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day to Crete: Take a ferry or short flight from Mykonos to Heraklion, Crete (ferry ~7–9 hours overnight or a 45-minute flight; flight recommended for time efficiency, ~€60–100). If taking an early flight, you'll arrive in Heraklion by mid-morning. Check into your hotel near Heraklion or in the charming old town.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Palace of Knossos (€15) – the legendary Minoan palace complex dating back to 2000 BC and one of Europe's oldest cities. Explore the fascinating ruins, colorful frescoes, and labyrinthine corridors that inspired the myth of the Minotaur. Hire an audio guide for context.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Heraklion's vibrant old town – walk along the Venetian harbor, visit the impressive Koules Fortress (€4), and browse the lively market street (1866 Street) for local products like Cretan olive oil, honey, and herbs.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the airport or hotel (€6–10)
meals.lunch: Traditional Cretan lunch near Knossos – try dakos (barley rusk with tomatoes and feta), Cretan salad, and local olive oil (€12–16 per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a traditional Cretan restaurant in Heraklion old town – try lamb with stamnagathi (wild greens), snails (kohli boubouristi), and local Cretan wine or raki (€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Knossos is 5 km from Heraklion city center – take bus No. 2 from Eleftherias Square (€1.70). The site is large; wear comfortable shoes and bring water. Book flights/ferries from Mykonos well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Drive or take a bus west to the Rethymno region. Visit the stunning Preveli Beach (Preveli Palm Beach) – a unique beach where a freshwater river meets the sea, lined with Cretan date palms. The hike down to the beach takes about 20 minutes and is worth every step.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the charming Venetian town of Rethymno. Explore the beautifully preserved old town with its Venetian lighthouse, Fortezza castle (€4), and narrow streets filled with Ottoman fountains and Venetian loggia. Browse the local shops for Cretan crafts and food products.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner in Rethymno's old town before returning to Heraklion (1 hour by bus or car), or consider staying overnight in Rethymno for a more relaxed pace.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your Heraklion hotel before departing (€8–12)
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch at Preveli Beach – pick up supplies from a local market: olives, cheese, bread, and fruit (€8–12)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a seafood taverna on Rethymno's Venetian harbor – fresh grilled fish, Cretan cheese pie (kalitsounia), and local wine (€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Renting a car for this day gives maximum flexibility (€35–50/day). Alternatively, KTEL buses connect Heraklion to Rethymno regularly (€7.60, 1.5 hours). Preveli Beach requires a short hike – wear good shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Crete: Visit the Heraklion Archaeological Museum (€10) – one of the most important museums in Greece, housing the world's finest collection of Minoan art and artifacts, including the famous Phaistos Disc and the Bull-Leaping Fresco. Allow 2 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend your last afternoon at Amnisos Beach or Karteros Beach – both are easily accessible from Heraklion (10–15 minutes by bus) and offer good swimming, beach bars, and a relaxed atmosphere. Enjoy a final swim in the warm Cretan Sea.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Heraklion for a farewell dinner. Pick up last-minute souvenirs – Cretan olive oil, thyme honey, and local herbs make excellent gifts. Enjoy a final Greek meal before preparing for departure.

meals.breakfast: Final Greek breakfast – fresh bread, local honey, Cretan graviera cheese, and strong Greek coffee at a café near the museum (€7–10)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a beach taverna – grilled calamari, Greek salad, and cold beer (€14–18 per person)
meals.dinner: Celebratory farewell dinner at a well-regarded Cretan restaurant in Heraklion – try the full Cretan meze experience with multiple small dishes, ending with loukoumades and raki (€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Check your return flight or ferry schedule and plan accordingly. The Heraklion Archaeological Museum is closed on Mondays – verify opening hours. Pack Cretan food products carefully to comply with airline regulations. Allow extra time for airport check-in.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Greece Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Sunset Sailing & Snorkeling Around Santorini Caldera
experiences.description: Join a small-group catamaran cruise departing in the late afternoon around the volcanic caldera of Santorini. Snorkel in crystal-clear Aegean waters, visit the Red and White beaches, and enjoy a traditional Greek mezze spread with local wine on board as you watch the legendary Oia sunset from the sea.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour (Varvakios Agora)
experiences.description: Explore the historic Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) with a local food guide in the cool morning hours. Taste cured meats, fresh cheeses, olives, loukoumades (honey donuts), and spanakopita. Learn about Greek culinary traditions and shop for local spices and ingredients. This indoor-friendly tour is perfect for avoiding midday heat.

experiences.name: Elafonissi Beach Morning Visit
experiences.description: Arrive early at the stunning Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete to enjoy its famous pink-tinged sand and shallow turquoise lagoons before the midday crowds and heat arrive. Wade across the shallow sandbar to the small island, collect sea glass, and swim in calm, warm waters. Pack a local picnic from a nearby bakery for a perfect morning escape.

experiences.name: Traditional Greek Cooking Class in a Cretan Village
experiences.description: Spend a morning in a family-run kitchen in a traditional Cretan village learning to prepare authentic dishes such as dakos (barley rusk salad), lamb with stamnagathi greens, and galaktoboureko (custard pastry). The class takes place indoors making it an ideal midday heat or rain alternative. Enjoy the meal you prepare with local raki and wine.

experiences.name: Evening Taverna Crawl in Nafplio Old Town
experiences.description: As temperatures cool in the evening, stroll through the charming Venetian old town of Nafplio and hop between traditional tavernas sampling local Peloponnesian specialties: grilled octopus, tomatokeftedes, fresh grilled fish, and local Nemea red wine. The cobblestone streets and neoclassical architecture create a magical atmosphere perfect for a leisurely evening of authentic Greek dining and culture.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 14:50
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) at 14:50 on Air Serbia. Clear customs, collect luggage, and transfer via private luxury car service to your hotel in central Athens. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll around Syntagma Square and the National Garden to begin soaking in the Athenian atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Gentle orientation walk through the Plaka neighborhood — the oldest district of Athens — admiring the neoclassical architecture and the illuminated Acropolis above. Enjoy a welcome dinner at a rooftop restaurant with Acropolis views.

meals.breakfast: Meal on board or at the airport
meals.lunch: Light snack at Athens Airport arrivals lounge or airport premium café
meals.dinner: Dinner at Strofi Restaurant (Rovertou Galli 25, Makrigianni) — a classic Athenian taverna with legendary Acropolis views; try the lamb chops, grilled octopus, and local Assyrtiko white wine

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange a private airport transfer. Confirm hotel check-in time in advance. Keep Day 1 light given travel fatigue. Athens weather in June is warm (~23°C) and mostly dry — perfect for evening walks.

day_by_day.morning: Early visit to the Acropolis and Parthenon (open from 08:00) before the crowds and midday heat arrive. Book skip-the-line tickets in advance. Follow with a visit to the Acropolis Museum, one of the finest archaeological museums in the world, housing original Parthenon sculptures and artifacts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Athens Central Market Food Tour (Varvakios Agora) — explore the vibrant historic market with a local food guide, tasting cured meats, fresh cheeses, olives, spices, and street food. Afterward, wander through Monastiraki flea market and browse artisan shops in the Psyrri neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Cocktails at a rooftop bar in Monastiraki with Acropolis views, followed by a refined dinner in Kolonaki, Athens' most upscale neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel or at a traditional Athenian café — Greek yogurt with thyme honey, spanakopita, and freddo espresso
meals.lunch: Tasting bites during the Varvakios Agora food tour; supplement with a mezze spread at a traditional ouzeri in the market area
meals.dinner: Dinner at Spondi (Pyrronos 5, Pangrati) — Athens' most celebrated fine-dining restaurant with two Michelin stars; Mediterranean tasting menu with exceptional Greek wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Book Acropolis tickets and the Varvakios food tour well in advance. Wear comfortable walking shoes and bring sun protection. The food tour typically lasts 3–4 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Ancient Agora of Athens and the remarkably preserved Temple of Hephaestus. Continue to the Roman Agora and the Tower of the Winds. Explore the Anafiotika quarter — a tiny Cycladic-style village hidden within the Plaka, with whitewashed houses and bougainvillea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided tour of the National Archaeological Museum, home to the world's finest collection of ancient Greek antiquities including the Antikythera Mechanism and the Mask of Agamemnon. Afterward, relax with a coffee in the upscale Kolonaki district.
day_by_day.evening: Evening at leisure in Athens. Enjoy a sunset aperitivo at a rooftop bar, then dinner at a celebrated modern Greek restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or brunch at Couleur Locale (Normanou 3, Monastiraki) — stunning rooftop café with Acropolis views and excellent coffee and pastries
meals.lunch: Lunch at Tzitzikas & Mermingas (Mitropoleos 12, Syntagma) — beloved modern taverna serving creative takes on Greek classics in a lively setting
meals.dinner: Dinner at Nolan (Voulis 11, Syntagma) — innovative Greek-Asian fusion by acclaimed chef Sotiris Kontizas; outstanding tasting menu with natural Greek wines

day_by_day.notes: The National Archaeological Museum is best visited in the afternoon when morning crowds thin. Consider hiring a private guide for a richer experience. Comfortable shoes essential.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Athens by private transfer or domestic flight to Nafplio in the Peloponnese (approximately 2.5 hours by car or arrange a scenic drive via the coastal road). Check into your luxury boutique hotel in Nafplio Old Town. Take a morning walk along the waterfront promenade.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the magnificent Palamidi Fortress — climb the 999 steps (or take a taxi to the top) for panoramic views over the Argolic Gulf and the old town. Visit the Bourtzi Castle, a small Venetian fortress on an islet in the harbor, accessible by short boat ride.
day_by_day.evening: Evening Taverna Crawl in Nafplio Old Town — stroll through the charming Venetian lanes and hop between traditional tavernas, sampling local Peloponnesian wines, grilled meats, and mezze as temperatures cool and the old town comes alive.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Athens hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch upon arrival in Nafplio at Aiolos Restaurant (Vassileos Konstantinou 30) — fresh seafood and Peloponnesian specialties on a lovely terrace
meals.dinner: Taverna crawl through Nafplio Old Town — start with ouzo and grilled sardines at a harbor-side spot, move to a wine bar for local Nemea red wines, finish with dessert (loukoumades) at a traditional kafeneion

day_by_day.notes: Nafplio is one of Greece's most romantic towns. Book a boutique hotel within the old town walls for the best experience (e.g., Nafplia Palace or Byron Hotel). The Palamidi climb is strenuous — go in the cooler afternoon or take the road taxi.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the ancient sites of the Argolid: visit Mycenae (UNESCO World Heritage Site) — the legendary Bronze Age citadel of Agamemnon, including the Lion Gate and Treasury of Atreus. Continue to the ancient theater of Epidaurus, one of the best-preserved ancient theaters in the world with extraordinary acoustics.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Nafplio for a leisurely afternoon. Relax on Arvanitia Beach — a small, clean pebble beach just a short walk from the old town, with clear turquoise water. Enjoy a swim and sunbathe before heading back to freshen up.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on a rooftop terrace overlooking the harbor, followed by a refined dinner at one of Nafplio's finest restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Nafplio hotel — Greek pastries, local honey, fresh fruit, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch prepared by your hotel or a local deli, enjoyed at the Epidaurus site; alternatively, lunch at a traditional taverna in the village of Ligourio near Epidaurus
meals.dinner: Dinner at Savouras (Bouboulinas 79, Nafplio) — renowned for the freshest seafood; try the grilled sea bream, shrimp saganaki, and local Moschofilero white wine

day_by_day.notes: Hire a private driver for the Mycenae-Epidaurus day trip for maximum flexibility. Bring water and sun protection — the ancient sites offer little shade. Check for evening performances at Epidaurus (the ancient theater hosts a summer festival).

day_by_day.morning: Depart Nafplio by private transfer to Athens airport (approximately 2 hours), then take a short domestic flight to Heraklion, Crete (approximately 45 minutes). Alternatively, take a scenic ferry from Piraeus overnight — but for a premium itinerary, the flight is recommended. Check into your luxury hotel in Crete (Heraklion area or Elounda).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Palace of Knossos — the legendary Minoan palace complex, one of Europe's oldest cities and the mythological home of the Minotaur's labyrinth. Hire a private guide for an in-depth experience. Afterward, explore the Heraklion Archaeological Museum, which houses the world's finest Minoan collection.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into Crete with a relaxed evening in Heraklion's old harbor area, exploring the Venetian Loggia and the Koules Fortress at sunset.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Nafplio hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a traditional Cretan restaurant near Knossos — try dakos (Cretan rusk salad), kalitsounia (cheese pastries), and local raki
meals.dinner: Dinner at Peskesi (Kapetan Haralampi 6-8, Heraklion) — one of Crete's most celebrated farm-to-table restaurants, serving heirloom Cretan recipes with ingredients sourced from their own organic farm; exceptional local wine list

day_by_day.notes: Book Knossos tickets and a private guide in advance. The site is best visited in the late afternoon when tour groups thin. Consider staying at a luxury resort in Elounda (e.g., Blue Palace Resort) for the remainder of the Crete stay.

day_by_day.morning: Traditional Greek Cooking Class in a Cretan Village — spend a morning in a family-run kitchen in a traditional village learning to prepare authentic Cretan dishes: homemade phyllo pastry, slow-cooked lamb with herbs, fresh cheese, and traditional sweets. Includes a visit to a local olive grove and herb garden.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive west along the northern coast toward the charming Venetian harbor town of Rethymno. Explore the old town's narrow alleyways, the impressive Fortezza fortress, and the lighthouse. Browse artisan shops selling Cretan olive oil, herbs, and ceramics.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Rethymno's atmospheric old harbor, surrounded by Venetian and Ottoman architecture, with the sound of the sea nearby.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before the cooking class (often included in the class)
meals.lunch: Feast on the dishes you prepared during the cooking class — a highlight of the trip
meals.dinner: Dinner at Avli Restaurant (Xanthoudidou 22, Rethymno) — a legendary Cretan restaurant set in a beautiful Venetian courtyard; try the slow-roasted lamb, stuffed zucchini blossoms, and aged Cretan cheeses

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class well in advance as spots fill quickly. Wear comfortable clothes you don't mind getting flour on. The drive from Heraklion to Rethymno takes about 1.5 hours — consider hiring a private driver for the day.

day_by_day.morning: Elafonissi Beach Morning Visit — depart early (by 07:30) for the stunning Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete (approximately 2.5 hours from Heraklion). Arrive before the crowds to enjoy the famous pink-tinged sand, shallow turquoise lagoon, and pristine natural beauty. Swim, snorkel, and explore the small island accessible by wading through the shallow water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Linger at Elafonissi through the early afternoon, then begin the scenic drive back east along the southern coast, stopping at the charming fishing village of Paleochora for a refreshing swim and a cold drink.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your Crete hotel. Enjoy a relaxed evening with a sunset swim at your resort pool or private beach, followed by dinner at the hotel's fine-dining restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your hotel before departure (pack snacks for the drive)
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a simple taverna in Paleochora on the return journey — grilled fish of the day, Greek salad, and local white wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at your luxury resort's signature restaurant — indulge in a Cretan tasting menu with local wines and end with loukoumades drizzled in Cretan honey

day_by_day.notes: Elafonissi is one of Greece's most beautiful beaches but gets very crowded by mid-morning in summer — an early start is essential. Bring snorkeling gear, reef-safe sunscreen, and plenty of water. The round trip is approximately 5 hours of driving — a private driver is strongly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Samaria Gorge — one of Europe's longest gorges (16 km), a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve in the White Mountains of Crete. Take the early morning bus or private transfer to the top entrance at Xyloskalo and hike down through dramatic scenery, wildflowers, and the famous Iron Gates narrows to the coastal village of Agia Roumeli. (Note: a moderate level of fitness is required.)
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Agia Roumeli beach — a remote, car-free village accessible only by foot or boat. Reward yourself with a swim in the crystal-clear Libyan Sea, a cold beer, and a rest on the pebble beach. Take the ferry to Hora Sfakion and arrange a private transfer back to your hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at your hotel. Enjoy a massage or spa treatment to soothe tired muscles, followed by a light dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your hotel before the gorge hike
meals.lunch: Lunch at a taverna in Agia Roumeli after completing the gorge — simple grilled meats, salads, and cold Mythos beer well-earned
meals.dinner: Light dinner at your hotel or a nearby restaurant — fresh grilled fish, horta (wild greens), and local wine

day_by_day.notes: The Samaria Gorge hike takes 5–7 hours. Wear sturdy hiking shoes, bring 2+ liters of water, snacks, and sun protection. The gorge is open May–October. If the hike feels too strenuous, substitute with a boat trip along the southern coast to the Blue Lagoon of Balos instead.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Crete by domestic flight from Heraklion to Santorini (approximately 45 minutes) or by high-speed ferry (approximately 2 hours). Check into your luxury cave hotel in Oia or Imerovigli — ideally a suite with a private plunge pool and caldera views. Take a morning stroll through Oia's iconic blue-domed churches and whitewashed lanes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Fira, Santorini's vibrant capital — visit the Museum of Prehistoric Thera (housing extraordinary Minoan frescoes from Akrotiri), browse the boutiques along the caldera-edge path, and enjoy the dramatic volcanic views. Walk or take the cable car down to the old port of Skala.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Sailing & Snorkeling Around Santorini Caldera — join a small-group luxury catamaran cruise departing in the late afternoon. Sail around the volcanic caldera, snorkel in the warm Aegean waters near the hot springs, watch the legendary Santorini sunset from the water, and enjoy onboard food and drinks.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Crete hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a caldera-view restaurant in Fira — try tomatokeftedes (Santorini tomato fritters), fava dip, and grilled local fish with Assyrtiko wine
meals.dinner: Light mezze and drinks included on the catamaran sunset cruise; supplement with a late dinner at Ambrosia Restaurant (Oia) — one of Santorini's most romantic fine-dining spots with breathtaking caldera views

day_by_day.notes: Book your Santorini cave hotel as far in advance as possible — the best properties (e.g., Canaves Oia Epitome, Mystique, Andronis Luxury Suites) sell out months ahead. Book the catamaran cruise in advance. Oia's famous sunset draws enormous crowds — the catamaran offers a far more exclusive experience.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the ancient site of Akrotiri — a remarkably preserved Minoan Bronze Age settlement buried by the volcanic eruption of 1627 BC, often called the 'Pompeii of the Aegean.' Hire a private guide for a fascinating in-depth tour. Afterward, visit the stunning Red Beach nearby — dramatic red and black volcanic cliffs meeting the deep blue sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax at one of Santorini's premium beach clubs on Perivolos or Perissa Beach (black volcanic sand beaches on the eastern coast). Enjoy a sunbed, swim in the warm Aegean, and sip cocktails with views of the volcanic cliffs. Alternatively, visit the Santo Wines winery for a private wine tasting of Santorini's unique volcanic wines (Assyrtiko, Nykteri) with caldera views.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Oia — Santorini's most picturesque village. Dine at one of the finest restaurants on the island as the stars emerge over the caldera.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel — enjoy it on your private terrace with caldera views; fresh fruit, Greek yogurt, eggs, and local honey
meals.lunch: Lunch at a beach club on Perivolos Beach — fresh seafood, salads, and chilled rosé wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Lauda Restaurant at Andronis Luxury Suites (Oia) — exceptional modern Greek cuisine carved into the caldera cliff with unparalleled views; try the lobster pasta and the volcanic wine pairing menu

day_by_day.notes: Akrotiri requires advance ticket booking. The site is covered and cool — a welcome respite from the summer heat. Rent an ATV or hire a private driver to explore the island independently. Santorini's roads are narrow and winding.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning on Santorini. Enjoy a long breakfast on your hotel terrace with caldera views. Take a slow walk along the caldera-edge path from Fira to Imerovigli (approximately 3 km, 1.5 hours) — one of the most scenic walks in Greece, with breathtaking views at every turn. Visit the Skaros Rock viewpoint.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last swim and relaxation at your hotel's infinity pool or a premium beach club. Do any final souvenir shopping — Santorini is known for its local wines, volcanic sea salt, saffron, and handmade jewelry. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Santorini Airport (Thira) for your onward flight, or if departing the following day, enjoy a final sunset dinner in Oia. Celebrate the end of a magnificent Greek journey.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent final breakfast at your hotel — full Greek spread with local cheeses, cured meats, pastries, fresh juice, and excellent coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Metaxy Mas (Exo Gonia village) — a beloved local taverna away from the tourist crowds, serving outstanding traditional Santorinian cuisine; try the fava, grilled lamb, and local wine
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Selene Restaurant (Pyrgos village) — Santorini's most iconic fine-dining restaurant, celebrating local Cycladic ingredients with a sophisticated modern approach; exceptional wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: The Fira-to-Imerovigli walk is moderately easy but involves some steps and uneven surfaces — wear good shoes. Book Selene well in advance. If departing on Day 13, keep the evening relaxed and pack the night before.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Greece. If time permits before your departure flight, enjoy one last Greek breakfast and a final stroll through Oia or Fira. Pick up any last-minute gifts — a bottle of Vinsanto dessert wine, local thyme honey, or handcrafted ceramics make perfect souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Santorini Airport (JTR) for your return flight to Belgrade via Athens (or direct if available). Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of ancient history, volcanic landscapes, pink-sand beaches, and world-class Greek cuisine.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Safe travels home.

meals.breakfast: Final Greek breakfast at your hotel — savor every last bite of Greek yogurt, thyme honey, and strong Ellinikos kafes (Greek coffee)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport or a quick bite in Fira before transfer
meals.dinner: Meal on board or upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Santorini Airport is small and can be busy in summer — arrive at least 2 hours before departure. Confirm all return flight details and arrange airport transfer in advance. Consider purchasing a case of Santorini Assyrtiko wine to bring home — many wineries offer shipping services.

query: Greece under $2000, beaches and local food, summer, flying from NYC
